headline: Just-in-time memory reports task-adaptive gains over write-time agent memory
summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces Just-in-Time Memory (JitMem), which stores successful raw agent trajectories and curates a compact, task-specific payload only when a later task is known. Across ALFWorld, WebShop and tau2-bench, the authors report gains over memory baselines, including 16.2 and 16.3 percentage-point success-rate gains over the strongest same-block learned write-time baseline on ALFWorld and WebShop. Gains on tau2-bench vary by domain: the reported increase is largest on Telecom, while Airline and Retail show no improvement beyond run variance. Results are author-reported and use multiple task orderings; they have not been independently reproduced here.
